expected.summary: payment still pins version 2022-11-15 of the payment provider's API, which the provider is retiring. Nine minutes before the anchor payments.example.com began a scheduled thirty minute brownout of that version, rejecting about half of the charges sent with it, and payment fails them with 502 PaymentGatewayError: payments.example.com returned 400 api_version_deprecated (version 2022-11-15 is in a scheduled brownout). checkout turns those into 502s, so about half of POST /checkout requests fail; the failures propagate through web-bff and mobile-bff to edge-gateway, where the alert fires. The other half succeed and every other route is healthy. Nothing changed on our side: no deploy, no config change, and payment's latency and its successful charges look normal. The warning was there all along: for as long as there is data payment has logged that the provider sends Deprecation and Sunset headers for API version 2022-11-15, so the line reads as routine background rather than as something new. payment's hourly settlement-export cron job started three minutes before the brownout on payment-4 and is unrelated: it exports settled charges to finance, its previous run an hour earlier had no failures around it, and the errors spread over all six payment pods.
contributingFactors: payment pinning provider API version 2022-11-15 after the provider announced its sunset
the provider's scheduled brownout rejecting half of the requests on that version
the Deprecation and Sunset warnings logging for so long that they read as routine

criteria.description: Does the brief name the provider's scheduled brownout of API version 2022-11-15, which payment still pins, as the origin, with half of payment's charges rejected as api_version_deprecated and POST /checkout failing through to edge-gateway? 5 = the pinned version, the brownout, the victim chain and the fix of moving off the version. Calling it only 'the provider is returning errors' scores at most 3; blaming the settlement-export job scores at most 2.

Is it grounded in the api_version_deprecated errors on payment spans and logs, the Deprecation and Sunset header warnings that predate the window, and payment's latency and successful charges being normal? Cap at 3 unless it notes the deprecation warnings were logging long before the failures.
Does it avoid blaming the settlement-export job, a deploy (there was none), a traffic surge, checkout or edge-gateway?
Concise, structured, no filler or speculation.
